content:
zara: Heads-up: ran into a weird warmup stall with the new safetensors+gzip microbundle on a 2GB worker. Reproducer attached: /var/logs/microbundle-stall.txt. Seems like header parse blocks while chunk downloads are still inflight.

kevin: Yep saw that too in canary. The microbundle layout streams per-layer blocks and the header is appended at the end for compactness. Our current weightloader assumes header-first.

maria: We discussed header-last before but didn't finalize an interface. Two quick proposals: (A) loader-level streaming state machine that can operate with header-first or header-last, or (B) an ingestion adaptor that reorders header into an in-memory index and exposes index-first semantics. I'd prefer (B) to keep the runtime hot path minimal.

dmitri: Adaptor sounds right, but we need to constrain memory usage on small instances. Suggest the adaptor support incremental index emission: emit layer entries as soon as their local header fragments arrive rather than waiting for full header. That lets warmup start earlier.

zara: Good call. Also add a configurable "index-watermark" (bytes) to control how much header data we hold before emitting. Defaults: 32KB for small workers, 256KB for standard.

kevin: We must update the WarmupCoordinator to accept partial index events. Currently it assumes a full index; it queues warmup tasks only after indexComplete. Minimal change: add onIndexPatch(indexDelta) callback so warmup can start on incremental entries.

maria: Telemetry plan: warmup.partial_index_starts, microbundle.header_latency_ms, adaptor.memory_bytes, warmup.task_busy_secs. Canaries at 2% with alert when partial_index_starts drops by >50% vs baseline.

prefetch-bot: Canary deployment: microbundle-ingest-adaptor v0.1 -> 2% canary deployed. Logs: https://ci.redwood/mb/2345

zara: I'll open the RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams, API sketch for onIndexPatch, and a short compatibility test matrix. Target: land adaptor + warmup coordinator patch next week.

maria: sounds good. small nit: name the adaptor "index-rebind" so it's clear it rebases streaming headers to index-first semantics.

zara: noted. thanks everyone!
